Summary of websites shared in #general:

• www.informations.com (shared by Bob) — A brief news item on the latest job report: unemployment edged down to 7.2%, bringing a mix of relief and concern.

• www.restaurant-zurich.com (shared by Eve) — Zurich Restaurant is a cozy, alpine-inspired eatery in the heart of the city, known for authentic Swiss cuisine such as cheese fondue, hearty rösti, and chocolate fondue. Warm wooden interiors with Swiss memorabilia, panoramic city views, and friendly staff in traditional attire make it feel like a journey to the Swiss Alps.

Hi Dora! I visited your personal website (www.dora-website.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- It's clean and straightforward — the page tells visitors exactly what it is right away ("This is personal website of Dora"), which makes it easy to understand at a glance.
- Including your e-mail makes it simple for people to get in touch directly.

Suggestions to make it even stronger:
- Add a bit more personality and content — a short bio, your interests, work, or projects would give visitors more to engage with than just a single line.
- Consider adding a few sections (e.g., About, Portfolio/Work, Photos, Links) so people have something to browse.
- A title or heading that stands out, plus some visual design, would help the site feel more polished and memorable.

Overall, it's a nice, no-fuss starting point — with a little more content, it could really come alive. Nice work!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I visited your blog (www.eve-blog.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- The intro is friendly and personal — "This is the blog of Eve" immediately tells readers whose space they're in.
- Mentioning that hiking is your favorite hobby gives a great hint of the theme and personality behind the posts, which is exactly the kind of hook that draws people in.

Suggestions to make it even stronger:
- Add some actual blog content — a few recent posts with titles, dates, and short excerpts would make the blog feel active and give readers a reason to come back.
- Since hiking is your passion, consider a "Hiking Adventures" section with trail write-ups, photos, or gear recommendations.
- A short "About Me" bio and links to your other profiles would help readers connect with you.
- A simple design with a header image or a photo from one of your hikes would make it more visually engaging.

Overall, it has a warm, authentic feel — with a bit more content and some visuals, it could become a really lovely little hiking blog. Looking forward to reading more!

Best,
Emma Johnson
